title: Gather molten glass from a furnace and shape your own cup or vase in one session
alt: A bright orange bubble of hot glass on the end of a metal blowpipe, with a workshop blurred behind it and the glassblower at the edge of the frame, face not shown.

posts.facebook:
Picture a glowing bubble of molten glass on the end of a long pipe, and you're the one shaping it.

At a glassblowing taster (a short beginner session), a glassmaker stays beside you. You gather glass from the furnace, add color and shape it into a paperweight, a cup or a small vase. The piece is cooled slowly first, so you collect it the next day or later.

Sessions run from under an hour to a full day, at studios in the UK and the US, and some take only two people at a time. Wear natural-fiber clothes and shoes that fully cover your feet, take off jewelry and tie back long hair.

What would you make first?

How to start, and where to go → https://dontdieretired.com/list/try-glassblowing/?utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=things-to-do
